sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the Adriatic Sea just east of the city of Rimini and is the southernmost part of the Umbria-Marche Apennines' outer thrust offshore. This is a NE-verging fault system at the eastern border of the Northern Apennines chain, parallel to the Marche coast.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show numerous damaging earthquakes that have occurred onshore of the area. However, one should note that the automatic treatment of the intensity data used to compile the historical catalogues places all epicentres inland by default, including the numerous cases where damage distribution convincingly suggests a more plausible offshore location. This is the case for the 17 May and 16 August 1916 (both Mw 5.9) Alto Adriatico earthquake doublet.
The presence of offshore splays of the Northern Marche blind thrusts characterizes the tectonic activity of this region. Subsurface data by Panara et al. (2021) have well-imaged offshore anticlines whose growth would be caused by the NE-ward advancing thrust. Various evidence suggests that the region just onshore is undergoing NE-SW trending compression, including earthquake focal mechanisms all along the outer thrust onshore (Frepoli and Amato, 1997), while borehole breakout data (Montone et al., 2004) illustrates a NW-SE trending minimum stress axis.
